title: The MettleUp sign-in is kept in plain app storage that Android copies into the phone's Google backup and onto a new phone
what: After a member continues with Google, the phone keeps the long-lived MettleUp sign-in in the app's ordinary settings storage, not in the phone's locked key store. That same storage is on the list Android copies to the member's Google backup and to a new phone during 'copy apps and data'. So the sign-in leaves the phone, unlike the member's AI keys, which are kept in the locked store and deliberately left out of backups. The code itself notes the locked store as the later plan.
expected: The sign-in stays on the phone it was made on, in the locked key store, and a restored or new phone asks the member to continue with Google again.
who: members who sign in with Google
how_often: every phone backup and phone-to-phone move while signed in
fix_line: Keep the sign-in in the phone's locked key store (as the AI keys already are), or leave that storage out of the backup lists

items.reason: The area calls 7 database functions and 1 table. member_copy_put, member_copy_get, member_copy_count, member_account_delete, join_gym_by_code and delete_my_cloud_data run only for a signed-in user (anon refused by test); app_limits is open to anyone by design and returns only the free-plan limits. member_summary is written through its row rule, which ties the row to the member's own id and own gym. The AI calls go straight from the phone to Claude, OpenAI or Groq with the member's own key; Drive calls use the member's own Google token. No fault.

member_items: one read rule, own rows only (member_id = signed-in user); writes only through the copy functions. Test proves another member gets nothing and cannot overwrite, and a gym owner reads nothing. member_summary: own row rule (own id AND own gym on write) plus a staff read rule limited to the staff's own gym and owner/trainer role. Test proves another gym's owner reads nothing and a member cannot write a row into another gym.
Rule applied: both tables the area touches (member_items, member_summary) have a test that proves another member or another gym is refused. No table without such a test.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only the catalog and the committed tests were read.

No key pattern hits in the area. The app carries only the public server key (guarded by row rules); the master key is never in the app. AI keys are typed by the member and kept in the locked key store, left out of backups.

No MettleUp AI key is inside the app: the coach uses the member's own Claude, OpenAI or Groq key from the locked key store, sent only to that provider, never logged, and the coach is switched off in code. Spend is on the member's own account, so no MettleUp spend cap applies.

Live sign-in is Google only (no password to guess); the old email-and-password path is switched off. The sign-in refreshes itself and the backup line shows 'sign in again' when it lapses. A sign-in from a different person than the one whose workouts are on the phone is refused. Password guessing limits are server settings, not in this area. Fault: the sign-in is kept in plain storage that Android backs up.

Text the member types (gym code, email, chat) goes to the server only as function arguments, never pasted into a query. Restore writes rows with fixed table and column names from the code and every value as a bound value, so a crafted backup file cannot change the query.

Nothing is uploaded to MettleUp's server as a file. The incoming file is the member's own backup: its size is checked, its list is capped at 64 MB, damaged files are refused, and every photo is written under a name made by the app (id cleaned or a fresh id), so a crafted file cannot write outside the photo folders. Drive restore downloads only from the member's own Drive.

The area's only code-based link is joining a gym by its code (old path, switched off in code), which uses the server function already found guessable. Gym logo and shop photos load from their saved link; no new guessable link here.

The libraries this area uses (server client, Google sign-in, app storage, locked key store, file access) have no entry in the dependency scan. The repo-wide gap that nothing warns about library holes is already a finding.
